key_insight: In forced stably stratified turbulence, interface coarsening is not random: vertical drift and merging occur when spatially uniform, vertically sheared helical structures emerge and break mirror symmetry.
engineering_relevance: Understanding when stratified layers merge versus decay helps predict mixing, layering persistence, and transport in geophysical and industrial flows.
method: Direct Numerical Simulations of forced stably stratified turbulence
Moderate-resolution runs integrated for very long times
Comparison across different Froude numbers and helicity-related diagnostics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that at low Fr (0.076) kinetic-energy excursions and interface drift coincide with helical structures, while at higher Fr (0.22) these structures are absent and interfaces decay.
watch_item: The conclusions come from moderate-resolution DNS and may need stronger resolution and broader parameter sweeps before generalizing to all stratified flows.
paper_title: Drift of interfaces in forced stably-stratified turbulence and the role of vertically-sheared helical structures
